title: Night Shift Rush

selected_top_5.reasoning: The player drives a car in real time, manages speed, steers through traffic, uses brake and turbo, and progresses through vehicle upgrades. The entire experience is built around arcade racing-style driving.
The run has no fixed finish line, distance is the main progression metric within a session, failure comes from crashing, and the structure is survival-based with repeated runs.
Although steering is analog rather than strict lane swapping, traffic placement and road design strongly revolve around four lanes and reading gaps in lane-based traffic flow.
The game includes acceleration, braking, steering, drift/handbrake behavior, and different car performance profiles, but it remains highly simplified and arcade-first rather than realistic.
Success depends on maintaining high speed, using turbo efficiently, and taking risks for faster earning and progression, even though the game is about distance survival rather than timed stages.

uncertainty_notes: There is overlap between 'Racing game', 'Endless runner', and 'Lane runner game' because the title blends traffic racing and endless-run survival structure.
The game is not a pure simulator, so 'Car simulator' is only a partial fit based on control vocabulary and vehicle handling.
Categories such as 'Neon runner' and 'Sonic style runner' were considered, but the car-based driving loop makes the selected five stronger matches.
